title: Overflow capacity safety net: metering, customer notifications, and soft-throttle semantics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers occasionally cross their reserved throughput briefly (minutes) during traffic spikes. Current behavior either exhausts reserve and silently falls back to hosted pool (surge pools) generating unpredictable invoices, or we hard-throttle which causes user-visible errors. We need a safety-net behavior that uses metered overflow capacity with transparent billing, a short-lived soft-throttle window for graceful degradation, and automated customer notifications.
goals: Make overflow capacity measurable and auditable by introducing a dedicated metering label for transient surge consumption.
Ensure predictable customer-facing outcomes: soft degradation (latency increase / partial throttles) before hard rejects, with explanation and billing visibility.
Minimize false positives where quota appears breached due to short spikes (seconds to a few minutes).
Provide operator controls to tune the safety net per-customer/fleet and an emergency off switch.
Reduce surprise invoices by surfacing rollover usage and projected cost before invoicing window closes.
acceptance_criteria: Metering: Overflow token usage emits metrics with label overflow_type=overflow_safety_net and is visible in per-customer usage panels.

Soft-throttle semantics: For the first 120s of sustained over-reserve traffic, runtime should allow requests with elevated per-token latency (best-effort) rather than immediate 429s; after threshold, progressively enforce rate limits.
Billing: Overflow usage is aggregated under a new invoice line item 'Transient Overflow (Safety Net)' and sample invoice preview available in Console within the billing dashboard.
Notifications: Customers receive intra-spike warning via email/webhook when projected overflow cost > $5 within 1 hour, with links to throttle/scale options.
Operator controls: Admins can toggle safety net per customer and adjust soft-throttle window and cost threshold via Console feature flag.
No regressions: existing dedicated throughput guarantees remain unchanged when safety net is disabled.
design_notes: Introduce a new runtime label (overflow_safety_net=true) that triggers a different accounting path in metering and a modified scheduler priority.

Soft-throttle implementation will prefer request admission with reduced concurrency and larger batching windows (to optimize cost) for safety-net requests while keeping latency SLOs for reserved lanes intact.
Billing pipeline will mark these tokens with a separate 'transient_overflow' product code; invoicing team will map that product code into a distinct line on invoices.
We need a graceful fallback from safety net to hosted surge pools only when both safety-net window and absolute capacity exhaustion occur to avoid double-billing or infinite fallbacks.
Console changes: new per-customer toggle and a projected cost estimator that uses recent spike patterns to forecast 24h overflow costs.
Operator emergency flow: a global kill-switch hidden behind RBAC and audit logs to disable safety-net for a particular customer if abuse is detected.
api_changes: Add new field in /v1/dedicated/usage -> overflow_safety_net: {enabled: boolean, window_seconds: integer, projected_cost_usd: number}
Expose overflow label in streaming events (event.overflow_safety_net = true) so customers can correlate responses to billing.
Console API: PATCH /admin/customers/:id/safety-net to toggle and update thresholds.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Enable safety net for <10 low-risk customers for 2 weeks; collect billing diffs and telemetry.
Phase 2 (staged): Expand to 25% of Dedicated fleets with automated backpressure if invoice previews increase unexpectedly.
Phase 3 (GA): Full rollout with default enabled for new Dedicated customers and opt-in for existing ones; two-week deprecation notice before forced enablement.
Backout: Global kill switch + automatic rollback of billing mapping if charge discrepancies exceed 1% at daily digest.
test_plan: Unit tests for new metering label and invoice tagging.
Integration test simulating 5-minute spike with varying shapes (sawtooth, steady, bursty) and asserting soft-throttle times and billing tags.
Load test with synthetic fleets to verify scheduler prioritization and latency impact on reserved lanes <1% regression.
E2E test that validates Console projected-cost estimator versus actual charged overflow in canary customers.
Security review of admin kill-switch audit logging.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers see unexpected charges from transient spikes. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, invoice preview in Console, 7-day grace credit for first-time overflow occurrences.
Risk: Safety net steals capacity from reserved lanes. Mitigation: scheduler priority ensures reserved lanes keep strict SLOs; safety net uses best-effort degraded paths.
Risk: Operator error toggles safety net globally. Mitigation: RBAC + mandatory two-person approval for global toggle; all toggles recorded in audit log.
